claude.sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 1,732 in combined cohort)
models_evaluated: Risk of bleeding complications after kidney biopsy prediction model (kbrc)

links.outcome: External validation discrimination and calibration of bleeding risk model against observed major bleeding
links.effect: External validation C-statistic 0.78 (95% CI 0.69-0.85), calibration slope 0.72 (0.41-1.02), calibration intercept 0.41 (0.02-0.80); Halifax bleeding rate 4.1% vs 1.9% and 1.8% in London.
links.quote: In the external validation cohort, the model showed good performance with an estimated C-statistic of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.69-0.85), calibration slope 0.72 (95% CI, 0.41-1.02), and calibration intercept 0.41 (95% CI, 0.02-0.80).

links.outcome: Model performance after recalibration in combined cohort versus original model
links.effect: Recalibration improved performance: C-statistic 0.84 (95% CI 0.79-0.89), calibration slope 0.82 (0.75-0.89), intercept -0.49; original external slope 0.72.
links.quote: Model performance improved with recalibration in the combined dataset; the estimated C-statistic was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.79-0.89), calibration slope 0.82 (95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and calibration intercept −0.49 (95% CI, −0.7 to −0.25).

links.outcome: Differences between development and external populations and effect on model performance
links.effect: Halifax cohort had more native biopsies (81.4% vs 40.1% and 35.0%) and higher major bleeding (4.1% vs 1.9%, 1.8%); model still discriminated well (C 0.78) with some miscalibration.
links.quote: The Halifax (external validation) cohort had a higher proportion of native kidney biopsies (81.4%) than the London cohorts (40.1% and 35.0%).

links.outcome: Model performance across sites and biopsy needle gauge subgroups
links.effect: Discrimination difference by needle size 0.005 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.10; P=0.915); performance at external site was good but slope 0.72 suggests some overprediction/miscalibration.
links.quote: Model performance is shown in Figs S3 and S4 ; a comparison of model performance showed a difference of 0.005 (95% CI, −0.09 to 0.10; P = 0.915), indicating no difference in discrimination between the subgroups.

models_evaluated: Risk of bleeding complications after kidney biopsy prediction model
Recalibrated combined-cohort kidney biopsy bleeding risk model

links.effect: 715-patient external cohort: C-statistic 0.78 (95% CI, 0.69-0.85); calibration slope 0.72 (95% CI, 0.41-1.02).
links.quote: In the external validation cohort, the model showed good performance with an estimated C-statistic of 0.78 (95% CI, 0.69-0.85), calibration slope 0.72 (95% CI, 0.41-1.02), and calibration intercept 0.41 (95% CI, 0.02-0.80).

links.effect: Recalibration improved performance: C-statistic 0.84 (95% CI, 0.79-0.89); calibration slope 0.82 (95% CI, 0.75-0.89).
links.quote: Model performance improved with recalibration in the combined dataset; the estimated C-statistic was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.79-0.89), calibration slope 0.82 (95% CI, 0.75-0.89) and calibration intercept −0.49 (95% CI, −0.7 to −0.25).

links.effect: Residual mild miscalibration above 25% predicted risk, where the model overpredicted risk.
links.quote: There remained some mild miscalibration in the probability range exceeding 25% risk where the model begins to overpredict risk, but this is likely of minimal clinical significance because patients carrying this degree of risk are typically not sent for biopsy.
